div.head: Cn 1020 2
div.ab: ⁊ ic cyðe eow, þæt ic wylle beon hold hlaford ⁊ unswicende to Godes gerihtum ⁊ to rihtre woroldlage.
⁊ ic cyðe eow þæt ic wylle beon hold hlaford ⁊ unswicende to Godes gerihtum ⁊ to rihtre woroldlage.
And ic cyðe eow þæt ic wylle beon hold hlaford and unswicende to Godes gerihtum and to rihtre woroldlage.
Und ich künde euch, dass ich ein gnädiger Herr sein werde und unwandelbar treu den Gerechtsamen der Kirche und rechter Satzung des Staates.
And I make known to you that I will be a gracious lord and unfailing in [upholding] God's rights and just secular law.
And I declare to you that I will be a gracious lord, and will not fail to support the rights of the church and just secular law.
And I inform you that I will be a gracious lord and a faithful observer of God’s rights and just secular law.
And I proclaim to you that I will be a gracious lord, devoted to the rights of the church and to just secular law.

note.seg: Æthelreds II. Breve, wodurch er Anfang 1014 um Wiederaufnahme in England unterhandelte, het gretan ealne his leodscipe ⁊ cwæð, þæt he heom hold hlaford beon wolde; Ann. Anglosax. Vgl. Gl Gnade 7. Die Treue hängt nur an Cnuts Person; dessen Haus bleibt unerwähnt, auch u. 56. S. o. Einl. 6

Æthelred II's writ, by which at the beginning of 1014 he negotiated for his readmission in England: het gretan ealne his leodscipe ⁊ cwæð, þæt he heom hold hlaford beon wolde; Ann. Anglosax. Cf. Gl Gnade 7. The loyalty attaches only to Cnut's person; his house goes unmentioned, also below, 56. See above, Einl. 6

Kirche und Staat in Ggs. auch u. 8. 9. Unter gerihta sind Kircheneinkünfte (s. d. Gl 2 ff., wie I Cn 8) nur zunächst zu verstehen. Er schärft Fürsorge für diese den höchsten Beamten u. 8 ein. Gerechtigkeit (s. d. Gl 1 ff.) und Billigkeit kündet Cnut als Regierungsgrundsatz u. 1027, 10

Church and State contrasted also below, 8. 9. By gerihta church revenues (see that word in Gl 2 ff., as in I Cn 8) are to be understood only in the first instance. He enjoins care for these on the highest officials below, 8. Justice (see that word in Gl 1 ff.) and equity Cnut proclaims as his principle of government below, 1027, 10
